topic: Verdant Aegis temporary overheal shield Memory
currentUserGoal: Add a ranked Memory that converts healing received at full Ancient HP into a temporary shield with satisfying visual feedback and bounded large-field performance.
workCompleted: Added Verdant Aegis as a ten-rank Touch Protection Memory branching from Green Afterglow rank 1.
At rank 1, 50% of overhealing becomes a shield capped at 8% of maximum HP for four seconds; the curve reaches 100% conversion, 35% capacity, and 6.25 seconds at rank 10.
Routed manual touches, Green Afterglow ticks, and natural healing through one allocation-free healing path so all eligible overflow can feed the shield consistently.
Applied Scourge damage to the temporary shield before Ancient HP, refreshed its lifetime when new overhealing arrives, and cleared it cleanly on expiry or Game Over.
Kept Run 1 deliberately unshielded even with debug Memories unlocked, preserving the intended first-collapse progression beat.
Prevented shield generation from counting as useful manual healing, so overhealing cannot be farmed for permanent Grass Touches.
Persisted exact shield amount, capacity, and remaining lifetime in active-field saves; legacy saves and contradictory Run 1 snapshots default safely to no active shield.
Added the Memory Web node, blue water-shield icon, rank costs, reveal rules, detail copy, semantic purchase control, status readout, and debug dataset fields.
Added a cyan-mint shield strip inside the HP bar, gain pulse, absorption flash, active shimmer, compact mobile copy, touch-summary feedback, and live shield state in the caretaker panel.
Implemented all Aegis animation state as fixed scalar values and existing pooled effects, with no per-heal timers, collections, or display-object growth.
Restored the browser playtest to a clean Run 1 after verification and left the local Vite server running on port 5173.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 194 Vitest tests across 23 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Targeted ecosystem system, Memory Web, and save verification passed: 69 tests across 3 files.
Memory Web geometry checks passed with 57 nodes: no connector crossings, node overlaps, blocked branches, or narrow shared-node branch angles.

Browser progression verified a clean Run 1 collapse, Tiny Sprinkler unlock, Heartwood and Green Afterglow prerequisites, Verdant Aegis purchase, shield gain from a full-HP touch, Scourge absorption, and expiry behavior.
Desktop 1280x720 and phone 390x844 captures showed readable Memory detail and active-run presentation with no incoherent overlap outside the intentional debug panel.

A 100x100 browser check retained 10,000 logical tiles, 100 rendered chunk views, zero rendered tile views, zero full-field scans, 83 visible display objects, zero frame spikes, and approximately 0.03 ms average frame work in the sampled browser state.
Browser logs contained no warnings or errors.
git diff --check passed apart from normal Windows LF-to-CRLF notices.

gitStatus.expectedAfterCommit: Verdant Aegis checkpoint committed locally; master is expected to be three commits ahead of origin/master and has not been pushed or deployed.

knownIssues: Verdant Aegis curves and costs are deterministic and browser-verified but still need hands-on balance feedback alongside Green Afterglow and Ancient Heartwood.
An active Green Afterglow stack can keep feeding or refreshing the shield at full HP; this is intentional synergy and should be judged in normal Runs 2-5.
The shield strip is deliberately thin so the primary HP bar remains dominant; hands-on testing may justify a small contrast adjustment without changing its layout footprint.
nextRecommendedSteps: Play Runs 2-5 normally and judge whether Verdant Aegis creates a useful safety window without making Heartwood or direct Care production irrelevant.
Tune conversion, capacity, duration, or Memory costs only from observed survival timing.
Push and deploy the three local master commits only when the user requests the next live release.
doNotRevert: Do not let Verdant Aegis activate during Run 1; the first collapse remains intentionally unavoidable.
Do not credit shield generation as useful healing or permanent-currency progress.
Do not replace the aggregate shield amount-and-timer model with per-heal objects or timers.
Do not add shield visuals whose pool or display-object count scales with logical field size.
Do not touch docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
